newsitem.title: USA: Calif. county toughens permit laws for refiners.
newsitem.headline: Calif. county toughens permit laws for refiners.

text.p: A California county's governing Board of Supervisors on Monday passed an ordinance that puts local oil refineries under tighter scrutiny when they shut for overhauls or maintenance, officials said.
The board in Contra Costa County, near San Francisco, approved the so-called "Good Neighbor" ordinance in a 4-to-1 vote.

Under the measure, local plants run by Unocal Corp, Tosco Corp or Shell Oil Co, could undergo review by several county committees before receiving a permit to conduct routine maintenance shutdowns known as "turnarounds."
The review process can last six months to a year, officials said.
Proponents said fires and leaks at local plants prompted the measure.
"In the last three years we've had a (chemical) release or fire at a major refinery every two-and-a-half months," said Supervisor Jeff Smith, who voted in favor of the measure.
Refinery officials could not immediately be reached for comment.
